answer: Proof-of-Elapsed-Growth Registry. An identity matures only by completing sequential, time-locked tasks whose answers depend on the prior step, like a vine that cannot skip a season. Each new identity must independently replant from seed and wait out the full growth interval; no shortcut transfers maturity. An attacker cloning identities pays the full elapsed duration per clone, since parallelism multiplies waiting, not speed. A comet event resets any cluster sharing a cedar-signed root, forcing restart. Cost: one full growth cycle per identity, unrecoverable.
